interim_updates.note_text: E.B. Creasy & Company PLC (Group) revenue fell 9% YoY to Rs 7,834mn for the quarter ended 30 June 2026, with Operating Profit down 36% to Rs 453mn, PBT down 51% to Rs 234mn, and PAT down 65% to Rs 105mn -- the company's own MD&A attributes this to 'local and global economic headwinds', Middle East geopolitical tensions, and a 100bps CBSL policy rate hike to 8.75% in May 2026 raising borrowing costs and squeezing consumer sentiment. By segment (60% Consumer / 20% Industrial / 19% Wellness & Nutrition of revenue), the Consumer segment's PBT collapsed from Rs 324.7mn to Rs 65.3mn (-79.9%), a swing of Rs 259.4mn that is larger than the Group's entire PBT decline of Rs 245.1mn -- meaning the other segments partially offset the Consumer collapse. Within Consumer, the Foods sector (28% of segment revenue) fell 24% to Rs 1.3bn from Rs 1.7bn on Middle East-related shipping disruptions that extended import lead times and caused stock shortages (since recovered per the MD&A), while Home Care & Personal Care (72% of segment revenue) grew modestly from Rs 3.2bn to Rs 3.3bn. The Industrial segment's PBT fell a smaller 8.3% (Rs 122.0mn to Rs 111.9mn) despite the Energy & Lighting sector's revenue dropping 47% (Rs 712mn to Rs 380mn, on grid connection limitations curbing renewable-energy project execution) and Building Solutions revenue falling (Rs 1.4bn to Rs 1.2bn, on lower GI wire sales and a shift to lower-revenue orders) -- the segment held its PBT relatively steady via cost management per the MD&A. Wellness & Nutrition was the only segment to grow both revenue (Rs 1.4bn to Rs 1.5bn) and PBT (Rs 51.8mn to Rs 52.9mn, +2.0%), driven by stronger demand for specialized nutrition and adult care products. Note the Group also re-presented prior-year segment allocations (Note: Segmental Information) with no impact on consolidated totals, and prior-year EPS (Rs 1.15) was retrospectively restated for the bonus element of a rights issue completed during FY2025/26 (shares in issue rose from 253.5mn to 278.9mn).

interim_updates.takeaway: The 65% PAT decline is overwhelmingly a Consumer-segment story: Consumer PBT alone fell Rs 259mn, more than the Group's entire Rs 245mn PBT decline, driven by a 24% Foods-sector revenue drop tied to Middle East-related shipping disruptions that the company says have since recovered -- so part of this quarter's weakness may be transitory rather than structural, though rising borrowing costs (CBSL rate +100bps to 8.75%) and consumer-spending pressure are cited as ongoing headwinds. Industrial and Wellness & Nutrition segments were comparatively resilient and should not be conflated with the Consumer-driven miss.

operational_highlights: Group revenue Rs 7,834mn, -9% YoY; PBT Rs 234mn, -51%; PAT Rs 105mn, -65%
Consumer segment (60% of revenue) PBT fell from Rs 324.7mn to Rs 65.3mn (-79.9%), the dominant driver of the Group's profit decline
Foods sector within Consumer -24% to Rs 1.3bn on Middle East shipping disruptions extending import lead times; since recovered per management
Energy & Lighting sector within Industrial -47% to Rs 380mn on renewable-energy grid connection limitations
Wellness & Nutrition was the only segment to grow both revenue (+7% to Rs 1.5bn) and PBT (+2.0% to Rs 52.9mn)
Basic EPS Rs 0.33 vs restated Rs 1.15 prior year; shares in issue rose from 253.5mn to 278.9mn following a FY2025/26 rights issue with bonus element
key_drivers: Consumer segment, Foods sector -- revenue -24% to Rs 1.3bn on Middle East-related shipping disruptions/import delays (per company MD&A, since recovered); segment PBT collapse of Rs 259.4mn is the single largest driver of the Group's earnings decline
Industrial segment, Energy & Lighting sector -- revenue -47% to Rs 380mn on renewable-energy grid connection limitations curbing project execution
Industrial segment, Building Solutions sector -- revenue down (Rs 1.4bn to Rs 1.2bn) on lower GI wire sales and an adverse shift to lower-revenue order mix amid heightened competition

Macro backdrop -- CBSL raised the Overnight Policy Rate 100bps to 8.75% in May 2026, raising borrowing costs Group-wide (interest expense per cash flow statement rose slightly from Rs 225.0mn to Rs 222.1mn despite higher average rates, suggesting some deleveraging)
